messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

Experiments so far (best first):
B3 | L8 | S3 | C2 | T2 -> 82.3%
B2 | L1 | S1 | C2 | T3 -> 28.5%
B4 | L12 | S1 | C2 | T2 -> 7.3%
B2 | L7 | S2 | C3 | T2 -> 0.2%
B3 | L6 | S2 | C1 | T3 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 20 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: This tests whether a lower temperature improves on the strong 82.3% result while retaining its other conditions.
This tests whether a higher temperature improves conversion with the validated base, ligand, and solvent.
This checks whether dilution improves the best-known conditions by limiting competing pathways.
This tests whether a higher substrate concentration improves productivity under the best-known conditions.
This isolates the effect of replacing cesium acetate with the bulkier cesium pivalate while preserving the successful catalyst environment.
This tests whether potassium pivalate can support the successful ligand and solvent combination.
This isolates the cation effect of potassium acetate relative to the successful cesium acetate condition.
This tests whether polar DMAc improves the reaction when the successful base and ligand are retained.
This evaluates whether a less polar aromatic solvent can outperform butyronitrile with the validated catalyst system.
This tests butyl acetate as an alternative solvent while holding the known successful conditions otherwise fixed.
This tests whether the bulky monodentate phosphine can benefit from the successful base and solvent combination.
This evaluates BrettPhos as a bulky electron-rich ligand under the validated reaction conditions.
This tests X-Phos under the successful conditions to assess whether its steric and electronic profile favors C–H arylation.
This evaluates GorlosPhos under the proven base and solvent conditions despite its distinct ligand structure.
This tests whether the sterically demanding tBPh-CPhos ligand supports higher yield with the validated conditions.
This isolates the effect of a smaller dialkylaryl phosphine in the successful reaction environment.
This tests PPh2Me under the best-known conditions to determine whether its intermediate steric profile is favorable.
This evaluates JackiePhos under the validated conditions to probe a bulky, electron-rich ligand alternative.
This tests triphenylphosphine under the successful base and solvent conditions for a direct ligand comparison.
This checks whether PCy3 can perform better when paired with the successful base and solvent rather than the previously poor conditions.
